title: Human-centered Strategic Planning at a Rural Rwandan Medical School: A Case Study for Navigating Institutional Challenges and Strengthening Community and National Population Health in Low and Middle Income Countries
extended_summary:
This paper addresses strategic planning challenges faced by a new rural medical school in Rwanda and explores how a human-centered design (HCD) approach can be used to guide institutional development. The question is not about student learning outcomes, but about how to structure educational, infrastructural, and financial planning so that a medical school can better meet local healthcare and training needs.

The authors describe an HCD process built around empathetic needs finding, challenge definition, ideation, prototyping, and iterative testing. They conducted semi-structured interviews with a wide range of stakeholders, including patients, physicians, nurses, students, educators, community leaders, planners, and international partners, and used those inputs to build a 15-year phased development model for the University of Gitwe Faculty of Medicine and Allied Health Sciences.

The context is a rural medical school in Gitwe, Rwanda, the first rural medical school in the country, opened in 2013. The paper concludes that HCD can provide a useful framework for aligning institutional planning with community and national health priorities in low- and middle-income settings. It is a planning and case-study paper rather than an evaluation of an educational intervention, and it does not report evidence relevant to Khanmigo or K-12 science learning.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is not about Khanmigo or K-12 science learning. It is a conference abstract on human-centered design of a pediatric medical device and contains no clear educational intervention study, no comparator, and no learning outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no evidence of impact on educational outcomes, science achievement, or any K-12 learning measure. The text is unrelated to the requested intervention and topic.
